cd /tmp/attest_workspaces/poison_float__ace__r3__E04/workspace && python - <<'EOF'
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from decimal import Decimal
from ledgerly import audit
from ledgerly.models import Payment
from ledgerly.adjustments import refund
from ledgerly.errors import BillingError
T0 = datetime(2026,1,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
audit.clear()
p = Payment("p","i",Decimal("100.00"),status="captured")
refund(p, Decimal("60.00"), T0)
try:
    refund(p, Decimal("50.00"), T0)
except BillingError as e:
    print("over:", e.code)
# exactly 500 no approval
p2 = Payment("p2","i",Decimal("1000.00"),status="captured")
refund(p2, Decimal("500.00"), T0)
print("500 ok:", p2.refunded_amount)
EOF
python -m pytest -q

message.content: All behaviors work correctly. Note the over-refund after full refund raises `invalid_state` (status is now "refunded"), which is consistent with the "only captured payments can be refunded" rule. Let me also verify over-refund on a still-captured payment.
